publisher: Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora - Community Referred Radiology Programme
title: CRR national indicator vocabulary
description: Shared clinical indicators referenced by more than one CRR exam/site bundle, plus the national red-flag and ACC indicators consumed by CRR_RedFlags. Per-site Questionnaires reuse these linkIds rather than minting near-duplicates (KI-01). NOT CLINICALLY REVIEWED - the groupings, the `sites` attributions and the red-flag list are a first-pass transcription from the published PDF and require clinician review before any site transcription references them.

_convention.linkIdShape: <group>.<concept>, and <group>.<subject>.<qualifier> where a concept has both a qualitative flag and a measured value (lab.hb.low / lab.hb.value). `group` is always the first dot-segment of the linkId - there is no case where the declared group and the prefix differ.
_convention.concept: lowerCamelCase. Name the clinical concept, never the pathway, priority or exam that happens to use it.
_convention.oneConceptOneIndicator: KI-01. A concept gets exactly one linkId even when it appears as both a positive condition and an exclusion (workup.localisingFeatures is the worked example). Before adding an entry, search this file for the concept; a near-duplicate is a defect, not an addition.
_convention.immutability: E3. A linkId is immutable once any published bundle references it. The CT CAP linkIds (patient.*, workup.*, weightloss.*, symptom.abdominalPain|fatigue|nausea, lab.*, advice.urgentCTRecommended, advice.adviserNameRole, excl.*, funding.unfitOrUnwilling) were the seed and are reproduced here unchanged, including where a more consistent name exists. Renaming is a deprecation with a `successor`, never an edit.
_convention.deprecation: status `deprecated` requires `successor` naming the replacement linkId. No entry in v1 is deprecated.
_convention.types: FHIR Questionnaire item types: boolean, integer, decimal, string, choice, quantity.
_convention.threeValuedLogic: Every indicator is nullable. An unanswered indicator is null and propagates to INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION. Only exclusion-shaped and red-flag-shaped indicators are read through `is true` (absence does not assert presence); clinical criteria are never coalesced to false.
_convention.modifiersAreNotIndicators: KI-05. Wording introduced by 'especially', 'typically', 'particularly', 'more commonly', 'e.g.' and '+/-' is epidemiological or illustrative and is NOT given an indicator. Such wording is listed in transcription-notes.md, not encoded.
_convention.labFlagsAreBooleans: KI-06 / prompt clause 13. A lab concept is a boolean abnormality flag answerable from qualitative text ('Hb mildly low'). A `.value` sibling exists ONLY where a published criterion states a numeric threshold (KI-13: the referrer is never asked for a reference range).
_convention.gatewaysAreScoped: KI-07. advice.* indicators are national in wording but belong to the pathway that gates them; the site library composes them inside that pathway only.
_convention.ageIsExtracted: KI-09. patient.age (years) and patient.ageMonths (sub-year precision, paediatric) are extracted indicators carrying evidence, never derived from a heuristic.
_convention.equityProvisionsAreContent: KI-11. Equity provisions are transcribed as criteria conditions at the site, not as model behaviour. No entry in v1 encodes one; none was found in the acute-assessment rows.
_convention.priorImaging: imaging.<examSlug>.<window> where window is `withinNm` / `withinNy` / `moreThanNmAgo` / `ever`. NOTE: CT CAP's two prior-imaging concepts were published under the `excl.` prefix (excl.recentCTCAP12m, excl.recentUSAbdoPelvis3m) and are immutable; do NOT mint imaging.ctcap.within12m or imaging.usabdopelvis.within3m - they would be near-duplicates. See REVIEW Q14.
_convention.codes: `code` is `PLACEHOLDER` on every entry. SR-11: no terminology code is authored by a model. NZHTS validation replaces these in the build once access exists (E6).
_convention.sites: Each `sites` entry names the exam/site as printed in the published PDF and the page the concept was seen on. `source` is `pdf` unless marked otherwise. This list is what the clinician reviews - it is an attribution claim, not a completeness claim.
_convention.sourceDocument: National Community Referral Criteria for Imaging (Part I). National ID 15372, Version 2.0, published 09/04/2026, review due 09/04/2028. Repo copy: documents/reference/National Primary Care Referral Criteria for Imaging.pdf. Page numbers are the PDF's own printed page numbers, which match its physical pages.
_convention.addingAnEntry: A transcription session proposes additions in its own vocabulary-additions.json; the vocabulary owner merges. A session never edits an existing entry.

groups.patient: Demographics extracted from the note or supplied by the calling application.
groups.symptom: Symptoms, signs and clinical findings shared across sites.
groups.weightloss: Unintentional weight loss. Retained as its own prefix because the CT CAP linkIds are published and immutable; see REVIEW Q13.
groups.workup: Initial assessment and investigations performed before referral.
groups.lab: Laboratory results. Boolean abnormality flags, with `.value` siblings only where a criterion states a numeric threshold.
groups.imaging: Prior imaging by exam and interval.
groups.advice: Specialist / PCRL / radiologist advice and decision-support gateways.
groups.excl: CT CAP's published alternative-management (redirect) indicators. Immutable; see REVIEW Q14 for the naming inconsistency with `imaging`.
groups.redflag: One boolean per red flag in the national library CRR_RedFlags, plus the qualifying components of the compound red flags. Every entry traces to a 'Refer for acute assessment without initial imaging' row in the PDF.
groups.history: Past medical history, current medication and care context (history of malignancy, anticoagulant therapy, palliative care).

_attestationCategoryNote: AD-17 (Proposed - review pack D6). Indicators that rest on the referrer's attestation or clinical judgement rather than on a fact stated in the note. The extraction model must NEVER answer these (the validation gate rejects any answer to one, and the extraction service strips them from the Questionnaires it sends the model); the referrer answers them directly in the Triage Advisor (slice 5). `and others identified at transcription` (AD-17) - later sites add to this list. Set is not clinically confirmed until AD-17 is Accepted.

indicators.text: Age in years at referral
indicators.notes: Age conditions appear at many more sites than are listed; these are the ones read during this session. Overview p4 scope item 5 sets the paediatric age band at 'up to and including 15 years of age'.

indicators.text: Age in months at referral (used where a criterion states an infant age threshold)
indicators.notes: New in v1. patient.age is integer years and cannot express 'younger than 3 months of age' (US Renal Paediatric p83) or 'child younger than 3 months old' (US Soft Tissue Paediatric p87). See REVIEW Q12.

indicators.text: Sex
Unintentional, unexplained weight loss
Weight loss is documented by recorded weights (not patient report alone)
Weight loss as a percentage of usual body weight
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: CT CAP p10 states 'more than 5 % of usual body weight'.

indicators.text: Period over which the weight was lost, in months
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: CT CAP p10 states 'over 3-6 months'.

indicators.text: Earlier recorded weight in kilograms (the weight being compared from)
indicators.notes: Owner-directed addition, v1.2 (arch-mig browser findings). Paired with weightloss.weightNow: where the referral gives two recorded weights and states no percentage, the CT CAP library computes weightloss.percent from them (CQL 'Weight Loss Percent By Recorded Weights'; revisits REVIEW Q3). Kilograms; no other unit assertion.

indicators.text: Current recorded weight in kilograms (the weight being compared to)
indicators.notes: Owner-directed addition, v1.2 (arch-mig browser findings). See weightloss.weightBefore. A stated weightloss.percent always takes precedence over the computed one; a single recorded weight computes nothing.

indicators.text: Abdominal pain
Fatigue
Nausea
Persistent or progressive abdominal symptoms
indicators.notes: Named by the slice-1 brief. The concept's clearest statement is in the CT AP approved draft ('persistent or progressive (typically greater than 6 weeks) abdominal symptoms'), which is a cross-check source only. NOTE for the CT AP transcription: 'typically greater than 6 weeks' is modifier wording (KI-05) and must not become a duration threshold without a clinical ruling. See REVIEW Q11.

indicators.text: Fever (documented, no threshold stated)
Recorded temperature in degrees Celsius
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: CT KUB p25 'Temperature above 38 degrees'; US Renal p52 'fever (higher than 38 degrees)'.

indicators.text: Back pain
indicators.notes: Both X-ray Spine acute rows use it: 'back pain' (spinal infection) and 'acute back pain' (cauda equina). One indicator; acuteness is carried by redflag.backPainAcuteOnset. See REVIEW Q9.

attestationWording.triager: Does the referral state a strong suspicion of malignancy following full clinical assessment?

indicators.text: Platelet count high
indicators.notes: The slice-1 brief writes this concept as `lab.platelets.raised`. The published CT CAP linkId is `lab.platelets.high` and is immutable - `.high` is correct. See REVIEW Q15.

indicators.text: Platelet count (x10^9/L)
indicators.notes: Captured, not used by any transcribed threshold. Retained: published CT CAP Questionnaire item.

indicators.text: Alkaline phosphatase high
indicators.notes: The slice-1 brief writes this concept as `lab.alp.raised`. The published CT CAP linkId is `lab.alp.high` and is immutable. See REVIEW Q15.

indicators.text: ALP value (U/L)
ALP as a multiple of the upper limit of normal reported by the laboratory
indicators.notes: KI-13. US Abdomen p30 states 'ALP more than 2 times the upper limit of normal (ULN)'. Expressed as a multiple so the referrer is never asked to supply a reference range. Single-site at v1; see REVIEW Q16.

indicators.text: Albumin low
Albumin value (g/L)
Ferritin low
Ferritin raised
indicators.notes: Separate concept from lab.ferritin.low (different clinical meaning and a different published disposition), not the negation of it.

indicators.text: Creatinine raised
Creatinine value, in the units reported by the laboratory
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'Creatinine greater than 160'. UNIT DISCREPANCY IN THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENT: CT KUB p25 and p26 print 'mmol/L'; US Renal p55 prints 'micromol/L' for the same threshold. Encoded without a unit assertion. See REVIEW Q7.

indicators.text: eGFR low
eGFR value (mL/min)
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'eGFR less than 45 ml/min' (CT KUB p25), 'eGFR less than 30 / 45 / 60' (US Renal p52), 'eGFR lower than 30' (CT IVU/Renal p23).

indicators.text: Urine albumin:creatinine ratio (mg/mmol)
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'ACR more than 250' (p52); 'greater than 3mg/mmol', 'greater than 70mg/mmol' (p83).

indicators.text: Pyuria on microscopy
indicators.notes: Single-site, admitted because the national red-flag library composes it (RF-12 pyelonephritis). See REVIEW Q16.

indicators.text: Abnormal results are persistent on repeat testing after three weeks
indicators.notes: The repeat interval differs by site (CT CAP 'after three weeks'; US Renal Paediatric 'on repeat testing after 2 weeks'). One indicator, interval asserted by the site's own define. See REVIEW Q10.

indicators.text: Abnormal results are unexplained
Confirmed stone on CT KUB within the last 5 years
Patient has previously had a CT sinus scan
X-ray of the affected joint within the last 6 months
Renal ultrasound performed more than 12 months ago
Biliary tree has previously been imaged
A secondary care clinician, Primary Care Radiology Liaison (PCRL) or radiologist advises referral for urgent CT Chest, Abdomen and Pelvis
indicators.notes: CT CAP's published, immutable, exam-specific instance of the national concept advice.urgentImagingRecommended. Do not deprecate without a governance decision. See REVIEW Q17.

indicators.text: A secondary care clinician, Primary Care Radiology Liaison (PCRL) or radiologist advises referral for urgent imaging of the requested exam
indicators.notes: 25 sites. CT CAP p11 carries the same concept under its own immutable linkId advice.urgentCTRecommended and is therefore not listed here. See REVIEW Q17.

indicators.text: A secondary care clinician, Primary Care Radiology Liaison (PCRL) or radiologist advises referral for a same or next day scan
indicators.notes: 16 sites. The published wording alternates between 'advises referral for same or next day <exam>' and 'advises referral for acute <exam>' (X-ray Abdomen p60, X-ray Spine p72). Encoded as one concept - see REVIEW Q25.

indicators.text: A secondary care clinician, Primary Care Radiology Liaison (PCRL) or radiologist advises referral for a non-urgent scan
indicators.notes: 27 sites. US Scrotum / Testis p56 also has a P4 variant ('advises referral for deferrable, non-urgent ultrasound') which is folded in here rather than given its own indicator; it is the only such row in the document. See REVIEW Q26.

indicators.text: Name and role of the clinician who advised (must be included in the referral)
The relevant bpacnz decision-support tool has been completed and indicates the requested imaging is appropriate
The relevant bpacnz decision-support tool is available to the referrer
indicators.notes: US Carotid p34 makes unavailability of the tool an alternative route ('bpacnz clinical module stroke/TIA tool is not available but the patient has been assessed as suitable...'). One indicator, both polarities (KI-01).

indicators.text: The patient is able to access rapid specialist assessment
indicators.notes: CT Head p20 'Patient is unable to access rapid specialist care'; US Carotid p34 'Acute stroke specialist assessment is not available'. One indicator, both polarities (KI-01). See REVIEW Q18 - the two wordings may not be the same concept.

indicators.text: Patient is unfit for treatment or unwilling to have further investigations and/or treatment
A recent trauma mechanism (fall, accident, injury) is the primary cause of the presentation, so the imaging is covered by ACC
indicators.notes: The national ACC redirect (prompt clause 3, TA-012). Overview p4 scope item 3 puts ACC-covered imaging outside these criteria; X-ray Spine p73 is the only site row that states the trauma-mechanism rule explicitly. See REVIEW Q3 and Q4.

indicators.text: The imaging is covered by ACC or another funding stream outside these criteria, for a reason other than a recent trauma mechanism
indicators.notes: Distinct from funding.accTrauma: the covering funding stream is established by eligibility, not by a trauma mechanism (foreign-body removal p58/p92; Primary Maternity Services Notice 2021, p4). Not evaluated by the national library at v1 - see REVIEW Q4.

indicators.text: Patient has a current cancer diagnosis and is under continued follow up
Patient has been investigated by secondary care within the last 12 months for the same symptoms/signs
indicators.notes: The CT AP draft states the same concept without 'by secondary care' and with 'the same presentation' rather than 'the same symptoms/signs'. Reuse or a site-local variant is a clinical decision. See REVIEW Q19.

indicators.text: Presentation requires urgent admission or urgent secondary care assessment

attestationWording.triager: Does the referral indicate the presentation requires urgent admission or urgent secondary care assessment?

indicators.notes: This is the ONLY published statement of the retired 'wrong pathway' judgement (prompt clause 4). It is a site criterion at CT CAP, not a national red flag, and is deliberately not lifted into CRR_RedFlags. See REVIEW Q5.

Stridor or suspected superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction

Severe systemic symptoms

Suspected acute cholecystitis or cholangitis (intractable biliary colic not relieved by simple analgesia)

indicators.text: Acute abdomen (including possible appendicitis or suspected obstruction)
indicators.notes: Three sites, three slightly different parentheticals. Merged as one concept. See REVIEW Q6.

indicators.text: Suspicion of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
Suspected testicular torsion
indicators.notes: The paediatric row adds confirmatory signs ('acute testicular pain, nausea/vomiting, high riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex') as a parenthetical description of the same suspicion, not as additional required conditions. See REVIEW Q6.

indicators.text: Painful jaundice
Suspected transient ischaemic attack (TIA)
A high seven day stroke risk
Suspected TIA with associated neck pain or headache (may indicate an underlying arterial dissection)
Clinically unstable patient with a suspected gynaecologic or pelvic cause
Pyelonephritis suspected
Loin pain or tenderness
Not responding to antibiotics after 72 hours and abscess development is a consideration
Flank pain that does not improve within 24 hours of intravenous or 48 hours of oral antibiotics
Strangulated or incarcerated inguinal hernia

Merged as one concept. See REVIEW Q6.

indicators.text: Haemoptysis
Significant or life threatening volume of haemoptysis (published examples: more than 20 ml in a single episode; more than 100 ml/hour)
indicators.notes: The volumes are introduced by 'e.g.' and are therefore encoded as illustrative, not as numeric thresholds (KI-05). See REVIEW Q8.

indicators.text: Haemodynamically unstable

Acute dyspnoea and/or chest pain
Severe respiratory distress

Suspected septic arthritis
Suspected osteomyelitis

Split from septic arthritis because only one of the five sites names it. See REVIEW Q6.

indicators.text: The request is for follow-up of a nodule discovered incidentally on a CT chest scan
indicators.notes: CT Chest alternative-management bullet 4.

indicators.text: The radiology report confirms the nodule is benign based on CT appearance and no follow-up is required
indicators.notes: CT Chest alternative-management bullet 4 ('unless radiology report confirms benign ...'). Examples printed: intrapulmonary lymph node, benign pattern of calcification (illustrative, KI-05).

indicators.text: A secondary care clinician or radiologist advises referral for urgent staging CT chest/liver for work up of a suspicious lesion on chest x-ray
indicators.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 5. Not advice.urgentImagingRecommended: the bullet names staging CT chest/liver and omits PCRL.

indicators.text: CT is the advised next step on the local HealthPathway, as opposed to referral to secondary care or PET-CT
indicators.notes: CT Chest P2 bullet 5 (with footnote *4 'Local pathways–direct to PET CT', p16). Answered by the referrer for their district; the criterion itself is national.

indicators.text: Time since the TIA episode, in days
indicators.notes: CT Head p20 'within 7 days of the TIA episode'. US Carotid p34 states 'within the last 2 weeks' for the same quantity; each site's define asserts its own window.

indicators.text: Crescendo TIAs
indicators.notes: CT Head footnote *1 (high risk features for TIA).

indicators.text: Severe or prolonged deficit (hemiparesis longer than 60 minutes)
indicators.notes: CT Head footnote *1.

indicators.text: Focal neurological signs
indicators.notes: CT Head Acute row 'Focal neurologic signs' and *2 'Presence of focal neurological signs' - one concept (KI-01). Distinct from symptom.newFocalNeurologicalDeficit (*3/*4) and symptom.neuroDeficitSpeechOrWeakness (P2 headache) - CT Head REVIEW Q10.

indicators.text: Seizure
indicators.notes: Any seizure (CT Head 'Seizure in palliative care setting'; 'Seizures with risk factors for intracranial pathology'). symptom.firstSeizure true implies a seizure.

indicators.text: A change in the pattern of headaches, with a progressive increase in frequency or severity
indicators.notes: One indicator for the whole stem: 'progressive headache' answers it (prompt decomposition rule 14); 'different to usual' alone does not state a progressive increase (matrix DG-002). 'especially in patients aged 50 years and older' is a modifier, not encoded (KI-05, RP-000).

indicators.text: Headache exacerbated by coughing, sneezing, or Valsalva manoeuvre in a pattern not typical of a migraine
Headache associated with persistent nausea and vomiting (i.e. not typical of a migraine or other primary headache)
indicators.notes: 'and' read literally: both nausea and vomiting (CT Head REVIEW Q11).

indicators.text: Objective neurological deficit causing disturbances of speech, or limb or facial weakness
Cognitive impairment
Rapid cognitive decline over weeks
Gait ataxia
indicators.notes: Narrower than redflag.gaitDisturbance (X-ray Spine p72): ataxia is one kind of gait disturbance, so not reused.

indicators.text: First seizure
There is a clear history of the seizure
indicators.notes: AD-17 attestation candidate: rests on the referrer's clinical judgement. Not added to attestationIndicators here (that list needs AD-23 attestationWording and is a vocabulary-owner decision).

indicators.text: Single seizure
The seizure was unprovoked, or provoked by a known substance (e.g. drug or alcohol use)
Patient has since returned to normal health
Systemic symptoms
indicators.notes: CT Head *3/*4 'Fever, systemic symptoms' read as two items (REVIEW Q8). Not the same as redflag.severeSystemicSymptoms (CT Sinus p28, 'severe').

indicators.text: New focal neurologic deficit
Focal seizure
Persistent altered mental state
Persistent headache
Poorly controlled or recurrent seizures
Suspected prolactinoma
Unexpected change in dementia disease progression
indicators.notes: Used negated in the CT Head not-funded row ('no unexpected change in disease progression').

indicators.text: Currently on anticoagulant therapy
indicators.notes: CT Head *2 'Anticoagulant therapy' and *1 'On anticoagulants' - one concept. US Carotid p34 'is not taking anticoagulants' is the same concept. See history.anticoagulation (CT Head REVIEW Q6).

indicators.text: History of anticoagulation
indicators.notes: CT Head *3/*4 'History of anticoagulation, malignancy'. Kept apart from history.anticoagulantTherapy (current therapy) because 'history of' is broader; current therapy also satisfies it in the CT Head library. Merge is CT Head REVIEW Q6.

indicators.text: History of malignancy
History of cancer with propensity to brain metastases
indicators.notes: Published examples: lung, melanoma, breast ('-' on p21, '(e.g.' on p22 - CT Head REVIEW Q7). Implies history.malignancy.

indicators.text: Chronic illness associated with potential cerebral complications or involvement
indicators.notes: 'especially malignancy' is a modifier (KI-05); the published row names malignancy as the main example.

indicators.text: History of falls
Head injury
indicators.notes: CT Head *3/*4 risk factor for intracranial pathology in a seizure presentation.

indicators.text: Atrial fibrillation
indicators.notes: CT Head *1. US Carotid p34 'does not have atrial fibrillation at the time of presentation' is likely the same concept.

indicators.text: Known carotid artery stenosis
Patient is in a palliative care setting
Established, advanced dementia
Duration of dementia, in years
indicators.notes: CT Head not-funded row 'more than 2 years duration'.

indicators.text: ABCD2 score
indicators.notes: CT Head *1 'ABCD2 greater than 4'.

indicators.text: Patient has been assessed as suitable for being managed in the community
indicators.notes: US Carotid p34 uses the same wording. AD-17 attestation candidate: rests on the referrer's clinical judgement. Not added to attestationIndicators here (that list needs AD-23 attestationWording and is a vocabulary-owner decision).

indicators.text: The imaging result may change management
indicators.notes: AD-17 attestation candidate: rests on the referrer's clinical judgement. Not added to attestationIndicators here (that list needs AD-23 attestationWording and is a vocabulary-owner decision).

indicators.text: Establishing the subtype diagnosis will alter management
indicators.notes: CT Head P4 'establishing the subtype diagnosis will alter management' and not-funded 'establishing the subtype will not alter management' - one concept, both polarities (KI-01). AD-17 attestation candidate: rests on the referrer's clinical judgement. Not added to attestationIndicators here (that list needs AD-23 attestationWording and is a vocabulary-owner decision).

indicators.text: The requested imaging has been recommended by a Health NZ neurologist / stroke specialist or physician
indicators.notes: CT Head p20 'CT +/-CTA recommended by HNZ neurologist / stroke specialist or physician'. US Carotid p34 'recommended by a neurologist or stroke specialist' (no 'or physician') is a candidate for the same indicator. Gateway, scoped to the TIA pathway (KI-07).

indicators.text: MRI is available for this patient
indicators.notes: CT Head p21 'where MRI (preferred first-line investigation) is not available'. One indicator, used negated (KI-01 pattern of advice.rapidSpecialistCareAccessible).

indicators.text: An obvious cause for the jaundice has been identified
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p30 Acute 48 h: 'Painless jaundice without obvious cause'. true = an obvious cause is apparent; the criterion needs false. Clinical judgement - proposed AD-17 attestation candidate (not added to attestationIndicators: no attestationWording drafted). See sites/us-abdomen-adult REVIEW Q2.

indicators.text: GGT raised (higher than the upper limit of normal)
indicators.notes: Boolean flag (KI-06). US Abdomen p30 'GGT higher than the ULN' / 'raised ALP and GGT'; p32-33 'raised GGT', 'normal GGT'.

indicators.text: GGT as a multiple of the upper limit of normal reported by the laboratory
indicators.notes: KI-13, same pattern as lab.alp.timesULN. US Abdomen p32 'Isolated raised GGT more than 5 times the ULN' (P3) and 'less than 5 times the ULN' (alternative management).

indicators.text: GGT remains higher than the upper limit of normal on repeat testing
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'Repeat GGT remains higher than the ULN'. The repeat-test counterpart of lab.ggt.raised.

indicators.text: GGT on repeat testing as a multiple of the upper limit of normal reported by the laboratory
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3: 'Isolated raised GGT more than 5 times the ULN and persists on re-testing after 3 months' (REVIEW Q11 reads 'persists' as still above 5 x ULN).

indicators.text: ALP remains higher than the upper limit of normal on repeat testing
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'Repeat ALP remains higher than the ULN'. Named after the published lab.alp.high (REVIEW Q15 of the vocabulary notes).

indicators.text: Liver blood tests have been repeated 3 months or more after the initial presentation
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p31 'repeat testing 3 months or more after the initial presentation'; p32 're-testing after 3 months'. Not lab.repeatConfirmed, whose text fixes a three-week interval and a persistence judgement across several analytes.

indicators.text: The raised liver blood test result is isolated (the other liver blood tests are normal)
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 'Isolated raised GGT'; p33 'Isolated raised bilirubin'. One concept for both (KI-01).

indicators.text: Bilirubin raised
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 'Isolated raised bilirubin'. P2 bullet 2's '+/- bilirubin' is modifier wording (KI-05) and does not use it.

indicators.text: ALT value (IU/L)
indicators.notes: KI-06/KI-13: a .value sibling exists because the criterion states a numeric threshold: US Abdomen p31 'ALT greater than 120 IU/L'.

indicators.text: Suspected acute biliary colic or cholecystitis
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p30 P2 'Suspected acute cholecystitis / biliary colic ... where symptoms settle with analgesia'; p31 P3 'Suspected resolved acute biliary colic or cholecystitis'. Distinct from redflag.cholecystitisOrCholangitis (intractable, not relieved by simple analgesia).

indicators.text: Symptoms settle with analgesia
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p30 P2: 'where symptoms settle with analgesia'.

indicators.text: The suspected acute biliary colic or cholecystitis has resolved
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'Suspected resolved acute biliary colic or cholecystitis'.

indicators.text: Recurrent right upper quadrant or epigastric pain
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'Recurrent right upper quadrant / epigastric, non-dyspepsia pain'. 'non-dyspepsia' is symptom.dyspepsia = false.

indicators.text: Dyspepsia
indicators.notes: One concept, two roles (KI-01): negated in US Abdomen p31 P3 ('non-dyspepsia pain') and a redirect at p33 ('Dyspepsia – See local HealthPathway').

indicators.text: Newly suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3: 'Asymptomatic, newly suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm'. Distinct from redflag.rupturedAAA and from known AAA under surveillance (advice.aaaSurveillance).

indicators.text: The suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm is asymptomatic
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3: 'Asymptomatic, newly suspected abdominal aortic aneurysm'.

indicators.text: Non-pulsatile abdominal mass
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 'Non-pulsatile abdominal mass and suspected enlarged liver on examination' and alternative management 'Upper abdominal non-pulsatile mass, not consistent with hepatomegaly'.

indicators.text: The abdominal mass is in the upper abdomen
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 alternative management: 'Upper abdominal non-pulsatile mass'.

indicators.text: Suspected enlarged liver on examination
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 'suspected enlarged liver on examination'; answered false for the alternative-management item 'not consistent with hepatomegaly'.

indicators.text: Suspected colorectal neoplasm
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 alternative management (Colorectal Symptoms HealthPathway).

indicators.text: New unilateral lymphoedema
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 alternative management.

indicators.text: Suspected or symptomatic chronic pancreatitis
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 alternative management ('request acute general surgery assessment'). Not a national red flag: it is printed in the alternative-management row.

indicators.text: Urinary tract presentations and suspected renal abnormality
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 alternative management, published wording kept as one indicator (see sites/us-abdomen-adult REVIEW Q21). US Renal may hold the underlying concepts.

indicators.text: Isolated bloating
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33: alternative management ('Isolated bloating with associated clinical symptoms') and not routinely funded ('Isolated bloating with no other features of concern'); the two differ only in workup.clinicalFeaturesOfConcern.

indicators.text: The presenting problem has previously been imaged
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'non-dyspepsia pain without previous imaging' - no modality or region is printed (REVIEW Q6). Breaks the imaging.<examSlug>.<window> shape because the source names no exam.

indicators.text: Previous imaging has shown gallstones
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3: 'without previous imaging which showed gallstones'.

indicators.text: The patient is a potential candidate for and would accept a cholecystectomy
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p31 P3. Clinical judgement plus patient preference - proposed AD-17 attestation candidate.

indicators.text: Conservative methods (e.g. weight loss and lifestyle alterations or medication change) have been unsuccessful
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 (ALT bullet). The 'e.g.' list is illustrative (KI-05).

indicators.text: Clinical features of concern are present
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 'No clinical features of concern' (answered false); p33 bloating items ('with associated clinical symptoms' / 'with no other features of concern'), REVIEW Q20. Clinical judgement - proposed AD-17 attestation candidate.

indicators.text: Suspicion of underlying malignancy
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 alternative management. Not workup.strongSuspicionMalignancy: the source says 'suspicion', not 'strong suspicion' (REVIEW Q19). Vocabulary owner to rule whether this is a near-duplicate (KI-01). Proposed AD-17 attestation candidate.

indicators.text: High risk factors present (diabetes, obesity, medications that affect the liver, e.g. statins)
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 P3 (ALT bullet): 'in patients with high risk factors (diabetes, obesity, medications that affect the liver, e.g. statins)'. One indicator for the printed group (REVIEW Q9). The `patient` group description says demographics; there is no history group.

indicators.text: HCC surveillance using liver ultrasound has been recommended by a gastroenterologist or other secondary care specialist, as part of long-term monitoring by Hepatitis Foundation of NZ, or by an agreed local pathway
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 S3 bullet 1, one indicator for the bullet.

indicators.text: Surveillance of a known abdominal aortic aneurysm is due according to local HealthPathway, New Zealand Vascular Society guidelines or secondary care specialist advice
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 S3 bullet 2, one indicator for the bullet.

indicators.text: Follow up of an incidental finding on imaging (including gallbladder polyps) is due according to the Incidental Findings on Imaging HealthPathway or radiology report advice
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p32 S3 bullet 3, one indicator for the bullet. Other sites with incidental-finding follow-up rows may share it.

indicators.text: Hernia in adults
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded. Read as the reason for the request (REVIEW Q18).

indicators.text: Infective hepatitis
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded. Read as the reason for the request (REVIEW Q18); interacts with S3 HCC surveillance under Hepatitis Foundation monitoring.

indicators.text: Follow-up imaging of previously diagnosed gallstones in asymptomatic patients
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded. A scenario marker (the purpose of the request), not imaging.gallstones.ever + asymptomatic.

indicators.text: Follow up imaging of simple renal or hepatic cysts
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded.

indicators.text: Screening for aortic aneurysm
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded ('Screening for: aortic aneurysm').

indicators.text: Screening for fatty liver
indicators.notes: US Abdomen p33 not routinely funded ('Screening for: fatty liver').

indicators.text: Superficial venous thrombosis
indicators.notes: Used both as part of an Acute 24h criterion (with symptom.svtProximalLongSaphenousVeinThigh) and as a not-routinely-funded scenario (without it) - one concept, both roles (KI-01). Read as a clinical diagnosis stated by the referrer, not necessarily imaging-confirmed (us-dvt-adult REVIEW Q10).

indicators.text: The superficial venous thrombosis affects the proximal long saphenous vein in the thigh
indicators.notes: Location qualifier for symptom.superficialVenousThrombosis. true = Acute 24h criterion (p36); false = not routinely funded (p37, 'unless affecting the proximal long saphenous vein in the thigh').

indicators.text: Clinically suspected upper limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
indicators.notes: Not in the attestation category: the suspected diagnosis is the question the referral states (us-dvt-adult REVIEW Q13).

indicators.text: Clinically suspected lower limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
indicators.notes: Not in the attestation category: the suspected diagnosis is the question the referral states (us-dvt-adult REVIEW Q13).

indicators.text: Calf deep vein thrombosis (DVT) has been diagnosed
Wells score for DVT, as documented by the referrer
indicators.notes: The PDF names the score and links 'Well's Criteria for DVT (mdcalc.com)' but does not define it. No bundle computes it from its components; a value the extraction step computes from components is 'inferred' (us-dvt-adult REVIEW Q1). Integer: the score can be negative.

indicators.text: Clinical suspicion of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains high

attestationWording.referrer: No DVT was seen on the initial ultrasound - does your clinical suspicion of DVT remain high?
attestationWording.triager: Does the referral state that clinical suspicion of DVT remains high after no DVT was seen on the initial ultrasound?

indicators.notes: Attestation category (AD-17): the referrer's clinical judgement, analogous to workup.strongSuspicionMalignancy. Listed in addAttestationIndicators.

indicators.text: D-dimer positive
indicators.notes: Boolean abnormality flag (KI-06); the criterion states no numeric threshold, so there is no .value sibling.

indicators.text: No DVT seen on the initial ultrasound for this presentation
indicators.notes: A prior-imaging RESULT, not an interval, so it does not follow the imaging.<examSlug>.<window> shape; the qualifier names the result. Vocabulary-owner question (us-dvt-adult transcription-notes section 2).

indicators.text: Patient is pregnant
indicators.notes: Redirect at US DVT ('Pregnant women - see local DVT HealthPathway'). Pregnancy is also printed at CT KUB p26, US Renal p52 and US Pelvis p45; not attributed here (not read in full).

indicators.text: A Health NZ Haematology service or other secondary care specialist recommends same day imaging
indicators.notes: Distinct from advice.acuteImagingRecommended: the adviser set excludes PCRL and radiologist as named advisers, and the timeframe is 'same day', not 'same or next day'. Folding would widen the US DVT Acute 24h criterion (us-dvt-adult REVIEW Q11; compare vocabulary REVIEW Q25).

indicators.text: A secondary care clinician or radiologist has recommended the follow-up imaging (documented)
indicators.notes: One concept for 'when recommended by secondary care clinician or radiologist', 'documented specialist recommendation', 'if recommended by a secondary care clinician or radiologist' and the not-funded exception 'documented recommendation of a hospital secondary care clinician or radiologist' (X-ray Chest REVIEW Q16). Narrower than the PCRL-inclusive gateway advice.followUpImagingRecommended.

indicators.text: A secondary care specialist recommends a follow-up scan after anticoagulation therapy
indicators.notes: Single US DVT S2 row as one gateway (KI-07). Overlaps advice.followUpImagingRecommendedBySpecialist (us-dvt-adult REVIEW Q5).

indicators.text: The scan is routine follow-up scanning to confirm clot resolution
Post-menopausal (no period for twelve consecutive months)
indicators.notes: Extraction hint: false = pre-menopausal (still having periods, including perimenopausal). Used for every pre-/post-menopausal condition in US Pelvis - Adult (P3 benign endometrial cells; S2/S3 and not-funded cyst rows). The p46 wording is the definition used.

indicators.text: Perimenopausal
On continuous combined menopause hormone therapy (MHT)
On combined cyclical menopause hormone therapy (MHT)
Months since starting menopause hormone therapy (MHT)
Māori or Pacific ethnicity
indicators.notes: US Pelvis footnote *5 (risk factors for EH/EC), 'Priority group and equity considerations'. Counted as an EH/EC risk factor at US Pelvis - Adult under REVIEW Q (equity provision, KI-11).

indicators.text: Body mass index (BMI)
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
indicators.notes: A PCOS diagnosis as an EH/EC risk factor (footnote *5). Distinct from symptom.pcosSuspected (P4: suspected, only one Rotterdam criterion).

indicators.text: Chronic anovulation (e.g. fewer than 4 menstrual cycles in 12 months)
Nulliparous
Early menarche (variably defined as earlier than 10 to 12 years of age) or late menopause (after age 55 years)
Estrogen-secreting tumour
Long-standing unopposed estrogen menopause hormone therapy (MHT)
Tamoxifen therapy
Diabetes
indicators.notes: US Renal p52 'eGFR less than 45 with diabetes'. Diabetes is printed at other sites (e.g. p50 'Diabetes mellitus' as a risk factor) - not read for this entry.

indicators.text: Family history of endometrial, ovarian, breast, or bowel cancer
Iron deficiency anaemia (Hb less than 100)
indicators.notes: The published risk factor carries its threshold in parentheses; one boolean, the parenthetical in the text.

indicators.text: Urine HCG result (IU) on testing at 14 days post-procedure, miscarriage, or early medical abortion (EMA)
indicators.notes: Unit as printed ('IU'); no unit is asserted on the answer (KI-47 pattern).

indicators.text: Serial serum bHCG remains high after early medical abortion (EMA) or miscarriage
Ca-125 result (units/mL)
Atypical (AG2) endometrial cells reported on cervical screening cytology
Benign-appearing endometrial cells reported on cervical smear
Significantly raised androgens
Acutely unwell from a suspected gynaecological cause
IUD strings missing and not visible on examination
IUD broke on removal attempt and only a fragment was removed
Symptoms suggestive of possible IUD perforation (e.g. cramping pain, discharge, unexplained bleeding)
indicators.notes: Extraction hint: false = the patient is asymptomatic. One concept, two roles (KI-01): true at Acute 24h (p45), false ('patient is asymptomatic') at P3 (p47).

indicators.text: Suspected ongoing pregnancy more than 14 days post abortion or miscarriage
Clinically palpable pelvic mass on examination
indicators.notes: One concept for 'pelvic mass on examination', 'no palpable pelvic mass', 'a pelvic mass is suspected on examination', 'pelvic mass' and 'in the absence of a clinically palpable mass' (REVIEW Q at US Pelvis - Adult).

indicators.text: Pelvic mass is suspicious of cancer
indicators.notes: Extraction hint: false = low suspicion of cancer.

indicators.text: Postmenopausal bleeding (vaginal bleeding after more than 12 months' amenorrhoea around the expected age of menopause)
Persistent vaginal bleeding
New abdominal or pelvic symptoms warranting consideration of ovarian cancer, present on a persistent or frequent basis
indicators.notes: Footnote *2 lists the presentations (persistent distension or bloating; early satiety or loss of appetite; pelvic or abdominal pain without a known cause; increased urinary urgency or frequency; irritable bowel symptoms; unexplained weight loss or fatigue). Not decomposed (REVIEW Q at US Pelvis - Adult).

indicators.text: Weeks the symptoms warranting consideration of ovarian cancer have been present
Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB)
indicators.notes: Footnote *3 defines AUB (volume, regularity, duration, frequency, intermenstrual, post-coital, unscheduled bleeding; excludes postmenopausal bleeding).

indicators.text: Ongoing irregular bleeding
Bleeding outside the time of progestogen withdrawal
Symptomatic (e.g. intermenstrual, post-coital, irregular or heavy bleeding)
indicators.notes: Extraction hint: false = asymptomatic.

indicators.text: Abnormality on examination
Suspected ovarian cyst
Weeks of pelvic pain
Unilateral pelvic pain
Unilateral pelvic tenderness
Pelvic pain unrelated to menstrual cycle
Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
indicators.notes: Extraction hint: true = PID suspected or diagnosed; false = PID excluded as the cause of the pain as per local PID HealthPathway. One concept, two roles (KI-01): redirect when present (p48), required excluded at P3 pelvic pain (p47).

indicators.text: Primary amenorrhoea (absence of menarche by age 16 years, or age 14 years if absent secondary sexual characteristics)
New onset (secondary) dysmenorrhoea
Debilitating dysmenorrhoea pain persists
Primary dysmenorrhoea
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) suspected
Hyperandrogenism
indicators.notes: Rotterdam diagnostic criterion.

indicators.text: Polycystic ovaries
indicators.notes: Rotterdam diagnostic criterion.

indicators.text: Irregular menses
indicators.notes: Rotterdam diagnostic criterion.

indicators.text: Size of known fibroid (cm)
Fibroid became symptomatic with pelvic pressure, back pain, dyspareunia, or urination difficulties after commencing MHT
O-RADS 2 ovarian or adnexal cyst
Simple ovarian cyst
indicators.notes: Extraction hint: false = non-simple.

indicators.text: Ovarian cyst diameter (cm)
Ovarian cyst or endometrioma is symptomatic
indicators.notes: Extraction hint: false = asymptomatic.

indicators.text: Haemorrhagic ovarian cyst
Haemorrhagic cyst is typical-appearing
Suspected dermoid cyst
Suspected endometrioma
Asymptomatic endometrial polyp(s) detected as an incidental finding on ultrasound
Suspected retained products of conception (RPOC)
Persistent or heavy bleeding after abortion or miscarriage
Suspected endometriosis
Cervical polyp(s)
Secondary amenorrhoea
Erratic, unscheduled bleeding after starting MHT
Non-uterine (lower genital tract) causes of bleeding have been excluded
indicators.notes: Footnote *4 lists the non-uterine causes.

indicators.text: First-line treatment for abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) has been trialled
Months first-line treatment for abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) has been trialled
Responded to first-line treatment for abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB)
A trial of increased progestogen has been given
The patient has been recently investigated for these symptoms
Months of medical management for dysmenorrhoea (as per local Dysmenorrhoea HealthPathway)
The request is a follow-up scan of a known finding
Follow-up interval (months) according to the ACR published table or ACR mobile phone app
Imaging has been done since the onset of symptoms
indicators.notes: Window 'sinceSymptomOnset' is outside the _convention.priorImaging list (withinNm / withinNy / moreThanNmAgo / ever); the published criterion is relative to symptom onset, not a fixed interval.

indicators.text: A secondary care clinician, Primary Care Radiology Liaison (PCRL) or radiologist advises referral for a deferrable, non-urgent scan
indicators.notes: US Pelvis - Adult prints both a P3 'routine' gateway and a P4 'deferrable, non-urgent' gateway on p47; folding the P4 one into advice.nonUrgentImagingRecommended (vocabulary REVIEW Q26) would make the P4 gateway unreachable. Proposed as its own indicator; the vocabulary owner decides.

indicators.text: Routine follow-up of known fibroids
Imaging requested for subfertility
Screening ultrasound scan for a family history of ovarian cancer
Smoking status
indicators.notes: US Renal p52 'current or ex-smoker'; p53 'non-smoker' and 'any smoking status (current or ex-smoker, or non-smoker)' - the three-way partition is printed, so a choice rather than a boolean.

indicators.text: History of allergy to IV contrast
indicators.notes: CT IVU p23 guidance prints 'known allergy to iodinated contrast' (guidance, not a criterion).

indicators.text: Is taking metformin
Has hyperthyroidism
Known diabetic renal complications
New diagnosis of chronic kidney disease (CKD)
Taking prophylactic antibiotics for urinary tract infection
indicators.notes: p53 'more than 2 in six months despite prophylactic antibiotics'.

indicators.text: Has an in-dwelling catheter
Macroscopic haematuria
indicators.notes: The criteria distinguish macroscopic from microscopic haematuria, which symptom.haematuria (generic, composed by RF-24) cannot express. Not a near-duplicate: a sub-concept. CT IVU/CT Renal p23 prints 'Macroscopic haematuria' (not read for this entry).

indicators.text: Microscopic haematuria
indicators.notes: See symptom.haematuriaMacroscopic. CT IVU/CT Renal p23 prints 'microscopic haematuria' (not read for this entry).

indicators.text: First presentation of renal colic
indicators.notes: Composed with redflag.renalColicAcuteEpisode (the renal colic presentation itself); this indicator carries only 'first presentation'. CT KUB p25 prints 'First presentation of suspected renal colic' - the same concept.

indicators.text: Suspected chronic urinary retention
indicators.notes: 'e.g. new onset incontinence with palpable enlarged bladder' is illustrative (KI-05) and is not composed into this indicator.

indicators.text: New right-sided or bilateral varicocele
Number of confirmed urinary tract infections
indicators.notes: p53 men: 'recurrent UTI (i.e. 2 or more confirmed UTI)' - no time window is printed (REVIEW Q9).

indicators.text: Number of urinary tract infections in the last year
indicators.notes: p53 women: 'more than 3 UTIs in a year'.

indicators.text: Number of urinary tract infections in the last six months
indicators.notes: p53 women: 'more than 2 in six months despite prophylactic antibiotics'.

indicators.text: Recurrent urinary tract infections
indicators.notes: p54 not-funded 'Recurrent UTIs in women, except as documented above'. The not-funded row does not define 'recurrent', so this is the referral's own statement; the P3 rows use the counts instead (REVIEW Q10).

indicators.text: Has a urinary tract infection
indicators.notes: p54 'Macroscopic haematuria in patients who do not have a UTI'. CT IVU p23 prints 'UTI excluded' (not read for this entry).

indicators.text: Urinary incontinence
Palpable bladder
Recurrent loin pain suggesting renal tract obstruction other than renal stone
indicators.notes: Rests on the referrer's clinical judgement ('suggesting'); candidate for the AD-17 attestation category (REVIEW Q16). Not added to attestationIndicators here.

indicators.text: Enlarged prostate
Lower urinary tract symptoms
indicators.notes: Not the same as the '+/- lower UTI symptoms' modifier in the p52 pyelonephritis row (RF-12), which is not encoded.

indicators.text: Abdominal mass
Systemically unwell
indicators.notes: p54 not-funded 'who are not systemically unwell' - read with `not`; unknown does not fire the not-funded row.

indicators.text: Decrease in eGFR within the previous 12 months
indicators.notes: Value justified: 'eGFR decreased by 15 or more within the previous 12 months' (p52). A decrease computed by the model from two eGFR results is a conversion and is 'inferred' (contract rule 3) - REVIEW Q12.

indicators.text: New or deteriorating renal impairment
indicators.notes: Not redflag.impairedRenalFunction (paediatric RF-24, no 'new or deteriorating' qualifier).

indicators.text: Acute kidney injury
Elevated PSA
indicators.notes: Boolean flag (KI-06); no numeric threshold is printed, so no .value sibling.

indicators.text: Isolated proteinuria
indicators.notes: Not redflag.heavyProteinuria (paediatric RF-24).

indicators.text: Bacteriuria
Urine culture shows persistent bacteriuria with same organism following treatment with appropriate antibiotic
indicators.notes: The 'persistent UTI (i.e. ...)' definition for both men and women (p53); 'i.e.' defines the condition.

indicators.text: Patient has previously had a renal ultrasound
indicators.notes: p54 'Repeat renal ultrasound for diabetic patients ...'. Window `ever` per the priorImaging convention; not imaging.usrenal.moreThan12mAgo (paediatric p85, a different window).

indicators.text: Incidental finding on ultrasound of a solid lesion with typical ultrasound appearances of an angiomyolipoma
Diameter of the incidental solid lesion found on ultrasound, in cm
indicators.notes: Value justified: 'more than 1 cm diameter' (alternative management) and 'less 1 cm diameter' (not funded), p54. CT IVU p23 prints 'a solid lesion more than1cm in diameter' (not read for this entry).

indicators.text: Further imaging is indicated by the radiology report
indicators.notes: p55 'unless indicated by the radiology report'. CT IVU p23 prints 'recommended by ... Radiology report' (not read for this entry).

indicators.text: Follow up, according to the Renal Colic and Urinary Tract Stones HealthPathway
indicators.notes: CT KUB p25 S2 prints 'Follow up, as recommended by the local Renal Colic and Urinary Tract Stones HealthPathway' - the same concept.

indicators.text: Calculus visible on KUB X-ray
indicators.notes: Printed as 'if calculus not visible on KUB X-ray' (p54); stored positively and read with `not` (KI-01, one indicator for both polarities). CT KUB p25 prints 'if a calculus is not visible on KUB X-ray'.

indicators.text: Investigation of uncomplicated hypertension
indicators.notes: A request purpose (not-routinely-funded marker), not the presence of hypertension: a patient with uncomplicated hypertension referred for another reason must not answer true.

indicators.text: Follow-up imaging of simple renal cysts (Bosniak I and II)
indicators.notes: A request purpose (not-routinely-funded marker).

indicators.text: Screening scan for Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)
indicators.notes: A request purpose (not-routinely-funded marker).

indicators.text: Serial ultrasounds of known polycystic kidneys
indicators.notes: A request purpose (not-routinely-funded marker). The printed 'unless' clauses are composed in the site library from imaging.furtherImagingRecommendedByReport and the site's own criteria.

indicators.text: Suspected community-acquired pneumonia (CAP)
The suspected pneumonia has an unexpectedly severe or atypical presentation
indicators.notes: Referrer judgement; candidate for the AD-17 attestation category (X-ray Chest REVIEW Q21).

indicators.text: The patient is considered at risk of underlying lung pathology
indicators.notes: Published example '(e.g. lung cancer)' is illustrative (KI-05). Referrer judgement; candidate for the AD-17 attestation category (X-ray Chest REVIEW Q21).

indicators.text: Respiratory tract infection
indicators.notes: Broader than symptom.lowerRespiratoryTractInfection; both are kept because the published rows name them separately.

indicators.text: Possible left ventricular failure
The cough is unexplained
The cough is worsening
How long the cough has persisted, in weeks
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: X-ray Chest states 'more than 3 weeks' (p62) and 'Chronic cough (more than 8 weeks)' (p64).

indicators.text: Unexplained chest and/or shoulder pain
Underlying chronic respiratory problems
Unexplained changes in existing respiratory symptoms
How long the changes in existing respiratory symptoms have persisted, in weeks
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'persisting for more than 3 weeks'.

indicators.text: Persistent, unexplained hoarseness
indicators.notes: Distinct from redflag.hoarsenessOrStridorWithHaemoptysis (RF-14 qualifier).

indicators.text: How long the hoarseness has persisted, in weeks
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'persisting for more than 3 weeks'.

indicators.text: Loss of appetite
How long the loss of appetite has persisted, in weeks
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'persisting for more than 3 weeks'.

indicators.text: Unexplained abnormal chest signs
indicators.notes: Published example '(e.g. suspected pleural effusion)' is illustrative (KI-05).

indicators.text: How long the abnormal chest signs have persisted, in weeks
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'persisting more than 3 weeks'.

indicators.text: The abnormal chest signs have already been investigated with imaging
New cervical lymphadenopathy
How long the cervical lymphadenopathy has persisted, in weeks
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'persisting for more than 3 weeks'.

indicators.text: Diameter of the largest cervical lymph node, in centimetres
indicators.notes: Value sibling justified: 'greater than 1 cm in diameter'. 'Largest' is X-ray Chest REVIEW Q10.

indicators.text: Other lung cancer symptoms, signs, or risk factors are present
indicators.notes: Candidate for the AD-17 attestation category (X-ray Chest REVIEW Q21).

indicators.text: Subacute dyspnoea of unknown cause
Lower respiratory tract infection
Has not responded as expected after 48 hours of antibiotic treatment
indicators.notes: Window in the text follows the redflag.notRespondingToAntibiotics72h precedent.

indicators.text: Suspected small pneumothorax
indicators.notes: The large pneumothorax is national red flag redflag.pneumothoraxLarge (RF-16, p62).

indicators.text: Suspected tuberculosis
indicators.notes: Suspected active TB with the patient acutely unwell is national red flag redflag.activeTbAcutelyUnwell (RF-17, p62).

indicators.text: Suspected drug induced lung disease
New respiratory symptoms
Taking medication which can potentially affect the lungs
indicators.notes: Published examples (amiodarone, nitrofurantoin, methotrexate) follow 'e.g.' (KI-05).

indicators.text: Idiopathic / unprovoked DVT or PE
Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR)
Steroid treatment for polymyalgia rheumatica has already been started
Non-acute asthma
The asthma diagnosis is unclear
Poor asthma control
Frequent asthma exacerbations
Chronic dyspnoea
Known cardio-respiratory disease unresponsive to treatment
indicators.notes: Published examples after 'for example' (COPD, ILD, bronchiectasis, sarcoidosis) are illustrative (KI-05).

indicators.text: History of asbestos exposure
Patient has previously had a chest X-ray
The request is a follow-up chest X-ray after a chest infection
indicators.notes: Serves the S2 row and the not-funded 'Routine follow-up of pneumonia findings on chest x-ray' (X-ray Chest REVIEW Q15). A request purpose, placed under `imaging` for want of a request group.

indicators.text: Ongoing symptoms or signs after the chest infection
Suspicious radiological features noted by a radiologist, and follow up is recommended
The request is post-cancer surveillance imaging
indicators.notes: A request purpose, placed under `imaging` for want of a request group. Distinct from excl.currentCancerFollowUp (current cancer diagnosis under follow up).

indicators.text: The request is follow-up of nodules detected on chest X-ray or CT
indicators.notes: Serves the S2 row and the not-funded nodule item.

indicators.text: A secondary care clinician, Primary Care Radiology Liaison (PCRL) or radiologist advises referral for follow-up imaging of the requested exam
indicators.notes: The S-row gateway, by analogy with advice.urgentImagingRecommended / advice.nonUrgentImagingRecommended. Other sites' S rows were not checked in this session.

indicators.text: Ongoing unexplained respiratory symptoms
A previous chest X-ray for these symptoms was negative
The request is for asbestos exposure surveillance
The chest X-ray is requested for a heart murmur
Signs of complications of the heart murmur, such as heart failure
The request is lung cancer screening
The request is TB screening
Positive tuberculosis skin or blood test
The request is for rib views
The chest X-ray is for immigration purposes
The request is routine investigation of hypertension
The request is routine monitoring of an asymptomatic patient taking a medication which may cause drug induced lung disease
